title: Untrack content file
description: A content file is either an app file (keyed by package) or a device file (keyed by target manufacturer).

localizedString.description: Text, keyed by language. English only. The object shape is kept rather than a bare string so that adding a language later is a schema change and a parser change, not a rewrite of every content file. See DESIGN.md on why the catalog is monolingual.

localizedStringArray.description: An ordered list, keyed by language. English only, for the same reason as localizedString.

media.description: A visual guide. Animated WebP only, committed under media/ and fingerprinted so the app can verify what it downloads. See media/README.md.

type.description: WebP only. MP4 would mean shipping a video player; GIF is worse than WebP at everything here.

sha256.description: Fingerprint of the file. The app checks it after downloading. Produced by: shasum -a 256 <file>

uuid.description: Permanent identity. Assigned once and NEVER changed — the app uses it to remember what a user has ticked off. Must be unique across the whole catalog.

id.description: Human-readable label, unique within this file. Safe to rename for clarity — nothing depends on it.

icon.description: RESERVED - not read by the app. Setting this has no effect on any screen today; it is kept so the field does not have to be reintroduced when app search grows logos. If you do set it, the file must be committed under media/ at exactly this path: a declaration pointing at a file that is not there is a broken reference inside signed content, and nothing at publish time will catch it. App names and logos are trademarks of their owners and are NOT covered by the content licence - only add one where such identifying use is appropriate.

osMin.description: Lowest Android API level in which this setting exists. This describes the SETTING, not the app: it is unrelated to the app's minSdk. Use null unless the setting genuinely appeared in a specific version. A value below the app's minSdk simply never filters anything.

osMax.description: Highest Android API level in which this setting still exists, for settings a manufacturer has since removed. Use null if it is still present.
